summary: Retained A's stable supporting-parent identity and same-world participation, then repaired five consequential boundaries established against A's cut: the P2Owner binding lockout, alias/stable-ID conflation with root/user identities, non-atomic registration partial states, a participation writer that trusted detached events and wrote partially, and actor access granted by a bare perception row. Registration and participation now commit as single C12 transactions; cold partials recover; the ordinary P3 reopen owner and a parent-scoped C01 owner compose. No second scheduler/owner/world/clock/ledger, no parent decision/utterance, no root replacement, no native authority.

Parent is a new stable supporting ID, not fixed A/B or the user actor; namespace collisions refuse.
Participation is recorded through actual C12 branch/world/perception machinery, not test-local state.

Duplicate registration is UNCHANGED with no new rows; duplicate episodes fail closed; replay is idempotent.
The ordinary root-scoped P2Owner (P3 reopen shape) and a parent-scoped C01 owner compose in either order.
No new owner, scheduler, person-world ledger, database or clock was added.
regressed_obligations: p2_owner.py byte change alters P3Owner._code_pins()/config_hash; pre-C01/pre-B01 state roots refuse cold reopen under the new code. Same-code roots reopen exactly; no migration invented.
C01 registration/participation remain origin-branch-bound; a C12 fork copies rows but reads refuse SUPPORTING_ACTOR_ROOT_OR_BRANCH_MISMATCH. Exact incompatibility preserved and tested.
A post-admission participation refusal can still leave the inherited P2 ambiguous reservation; E03 owns composite event+participation recovery.
No full-estate run; the pre-existing P6 chronology-proof failure and full P3 vertical-slice timeout are untouched.

defects_repaired.title: P2Owner binding lockout across participant scopes
defects_repaired.evidence: Root-scoped owner then parent-scoped owner and the reverse both refused P2_OWNER_BINDING_MISMATCH on A HEAD 7e347c45d; the ordinary P3 reopen shape uses tuple(root actor_ids).
defects_repaired.repair: Persist root_participants as the invariant; migrate legacy participant rows; validate declared participants live.

defects_repaired.title: Alias/stable-ID conflation with root or user identity
defects_repaired.evidence: alias=root stable ID registered and read_actor_access resolved the root actor; actor_id='U' registered and read_actor_access('U') resolved the user actor.

defects_repaired.title: Non-atomic registration; cold ghost branch alias
defects_repaired.evidence: Branch actor update committed before episode/world checkpoint; cold reopen left branch actor_ids containing P with no world row and re-registration refused ALIAS_RESERVED forever.
defects_repaired.repair: One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction for branch+episode+checkpoint; cold recovery of partial episode/branch-only states; duplicate-episode detection.

defects_repaired.title: Participation writer trusted a format-valid event and wrote partially
defects_repaired.evidence: Forged hash/clock/kind event mapping produced a participation episode with forged values; per-participant writes could leave a first actor recorded when a later participant refused.
defects_repaired.repair: Resolve the actual store event and require canonical equality; pre-validate all participants; one transaction for all receipts/episodes.

defects_repaired.title: Bare perception row granted actor access
defects_repaired.evidence: A manually inserted C12 perception row for the parent with no participation episode returned PERCEIVED; severing the participation episode did not change the read.
defects_repaired.repair: Supporting access requires registration + participation episode + co_present receipt at the event clock/channel; bare/severed/forged receipts refuse.
